title: Problem A · from a file every minute to one clear decision

rows.why: Files are our own and simple; paid connectors charge per row, and 1,440 files a day adds up
rows.giveUp: We own fixes when a file's format changes
rows.swapPlan: Each source has one small checker function; a managed connector could replace the trigger later without touching the checks.
rows.costAt10x: Storage and checking grow in a straight line with the number of files, and checks run in parallel, so nothing needs a redesign.

rows.decision: Buy (managed columnar, for example hosted ClickHouse)
rows.why: Running one is a full-time job; standard SQL keeps us portable
rows.giveUp: A monthly bill and some vendor dependence
rows.swapPlan: Standard SQL and open file formats: the roll-ups can be re-pointed at another columnar store in one migration project.
rows.costAt10x: Storage grows 10×, but questions read hourly and daily roll-ups, so compute grows far less than the raw volume.

rows.why: It's the truth of the business and can't live in a tool we don't control
rows.swapPlan: Definitions live as versioned code in our repository; every database and BI tool reads them, so there is nothing to swap.
rows.costAt10x: No change: definitions grow with the number of metrics, not with the volume of data.

rows.why: Easy to explain, fast, catches most real problems
rows.giveUp: Misses subtle patterns that heavy ML might find
rows.swapPlan: Baselines sit behind one 'is this unusual?' check; a learned model can replace them metric by metric after running side by side.
rows.costAt10x: Baselines are prepared per store and hour of the week, so 10× more stores means 10× small tables that still refresh in minutes.

rows.component: The AI that writes the text
rows.why: Training our own is slow and costly; our edge is data and checks
rows.giveUp: Cost per report; we send only totals, never personal data
rows.swapPlan: One prompt and one number checker around a provider-neutral call: switching models is a config change plus an evaluation run.
rows.costAt10x: Reports are per team, not per row: 10× more data still means the same number of reports, so AI cost barely moves.

rows.decision: Buy (standard BI tool, for example Metabase)
rows.why: Analysts need freedom; building it is wasted effort
rows.giveUp: Two places to look, so the report links into the BI tool
rows.swapPlan: It reads the same shared definitions, so another BI tool can replace it without changing a single number.
rows.costAt10x: Priced by seat, not by data, so 10× the volume leaves the bill where it is.
